newsitem.title: USA: FPL sues dying man for legal fees - report.
newsitem.headline: FPL sues dying man for legal fees - report.

text.p: FPL Group Inc's Florida Power & Light Co has sued a former principal who is dying of cancer, demanding more than a quarter-million dollars that the utility said it spent to fight the educator's lawsuit, which alleged FP&L power lines carried dangerous levels of radiation, according to a Mimi Herald report.
Leonard Glazer lost a lawsuit last May against the utility that claimed FP&L's power lines above his house caused the leukemia that killed his wife and is now killing him.

In court papers filed on Friday, the utility said it wanted Glazer to repay $267,885.26 of the costs of the lawsuit. "Why should FPL pay for being sued, especially when it would come right out of the ratepayers' pockets?" FP&L attorney Alvin Davis told the Miami Herald. "We told them from the beginning that they didn't have a case and if they pursued it, they'd face the consequences," he added.
Glazer, 59, said his doctors have given him a 50-50 chance of surviving until the end of the year.
A former high school principal in Miami, Glazer alleged in his lawsuit that the electromagnetic fields from FP&L's power lines above his house caused the leukemia.
The utility maintained that the power lines had nothing to do with the leukemia contracted by Glazer and his wife, Elsa. She died in 1988.

Earlier this year, a Dade County court judge ruled that the amount of radiation from the transmission lines was not harmful. Glazer appealed the case, and it is scheduled to be argued before a state appeals court in November.
In defending itself from the lawsuit, FP&L spent more than $400,000 to pay expert witnesses to testify that the power lines were safe, the report said.
